headline: Noskova wastes five championship points, then wins Wimbledon anyway
whyCareReason: A 21-year-old from a village of a thousand people becomes the youngest women's Wimbledon champion since Kvitova in 2011.
teaser: Linda Noskova def. Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3. All-Czech final. First Slam. Converted the sixth championship point.
story:
Why this one matters: Wimbledon finals are supposed to belong to the names you already know. On 11 July the names were Czech, seeded 9 and 10, and friends.

Noskova led 6-2, 5-2. Muchova won five games in a row, saved five championship points, forced a decider. Noskova reset and won 6-3 in the third, converting a sixth championship point with a service winner after an ace. BBC, The Athletic and CBS all logged the same score: 6-2, 5-7, 6-3.

She is 21. Youngest women's champion here since Petra Kvitova in 2011. First Slam. She also won Berlin on the grass before she arrived. Prize money around $4.8 million, nearly doubling her career on-court earnings.
stakes: A first major, an all-Czech final, a new name on the board.
rivalryAngle: Friends, same country, opposite sides of Centre Court.
